data.title: Exploring AI Integrations with Adobe Photoshop, InDesign and Premiere Pro
data.author: mesh
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了AI与Adobe Photoshop、InDesign和Premiere Pro的整合可能性。作者介绍了开源项目**adb-mcp**，它通过MCP服务器让AI控制这些Adobe应用。目前，Photoshop功能最完善，Premiere Pro和InDesign则分别处于beta测试和基础功能阶段。整合通过一个Python MCP服务器、一个Node代理服务器和UXP插件实现，AI发送命令后由插件执行。虽然这是一个概念验证项目，且需要一些命令行知识，但它展示了AI在创意工作流中的潜力，比如自动重命名图层、创建幻灯片和音乐视频等。未来改进包括简化设置过程、避免文件系统传输图像以及让UXP插件支持socket监听。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[使用ChatGPT 4与Photoshop等Adobe软件进行脚本开发的可行性及相关工具的限制]

不同观点：
• [tmaly] 认为ChatGPT 4可以用于构建简单的脚本，通过Photoshop的JavaScript接口来实现。这表明他对该技术结合持积极态度，并认可ChatGPT在简化开发过程中的潜力。

• [F7F7F7] 对需要通过视频来理解实现结果的方式表示不满，更倾向于书面内容。同时，他提到在66%的情况下，结果是以栅格和矢量形式呈现，暗示这些技术在实际应用中仍有局限性，特别是在信息传递和理解方面。

• [Jayakumark] 对使用Adobe UXP API表示了一定的失望，特别是对于Premiere Pro中缺乏对CEP功能的支持，如MOGRT和Transcript数据支持。他希望这些问题能尽快得到解决，显示出对Adobe工具当前功能限制的不满，同时期待改进。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了不同工具之间的功能差异和限制，如UXP和CEP，以及这些差异如何影响实际应用。
• 不同用户对技术实现和信息呈现方式的偏好各异，有的用户偏好文字说明，而有的则可能接受视频演示。
• 争议的焦点可能在于现有工具的局限性和用户对功能改进的期望之间的差距，尤其是在专业软件如Premiere Pro中的功能缺失。

44201519.article_content:
Exploring AI Integrations with Adobe Photoshop, InDesign and Premiere Pro
June 6, 2025
As I expect most people in the tech industry have been doing, Iâve been spending a lot of time lately thinking about AI and its impact. As I work with the community for Adobe, I’ve specifically been thinking about how it will affect the creative industry, and its implications for Adobe and Adobeâs creative tools.
Adobe makes industry leading creative tools such as Photoshop, Illustrator and Premiere Pro, and I have been curious about exploring how / if these tools fit in within an AI first world. While I definitely have some thoughts on that (Iâll save that for another post), I wanted to start with the basics and explore how and if Adobe tools could be integrated with AI tools. Questions like:
Can they be integrated with and controlled by AI?
What types of roles and tasks would it be useful for?
Could AI be used as a glorified scripting language?
Could it be used to do the actual creation (similar to generative AI)?
What are the barriers given current technical constraints to adoption?
There has been a lot of buzz around MCP servers over the past couple of months with integrations with other creative tools / frameworks like Blender and Unity, that showed that AI could be used to drive these types of creative workflows. I started to look at whether it would be possible to hook up Adobe apps such as Photoshop in a similar way and it turns out that yes, you can! And even better, everything needed is publicly available.
Adobe Creative App MCP Server
adb-mcp
Introducing adb-mcp, an open source project that provides MCP servers to enable AI clients and agents to control Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Premiere Pro and Adobe InDesign.
https://github.com/mikechambers/adb-mcp
Currently, there are plugins for three Adobe apps:
Adobe Photoshop : Has the most functionality exposed
Adobe Premiere Pro : UXP support is in beta, and thus mostly just basic functionality is exposed
Adobe InDesign : Has extensive UXP support, but I have only implemented basic document creation thus far
Note:
This is a proof of concept project, and is not supported by, nor endorsed by Adobe.
This has been tested using Claude Desktop, as well as custom agents, but in general should work with any client / code that supports MCP. In addition, any Adobe app that supports the UXP plugin API should be easy to add support for (it may also be technically possible to add support for other apps, but I havenât looked into it).
How does it work?
It works by providing:
A Python based MCP Server that provides an interface to functionality within Adobe Photoshop to the AI
A Node based command proxy server that sits between the MCP server and Adobe app plugins
An UXP based Adobe app (Photoshop, Premiere & InDesign) plugin that listens for and executes commands from the AI
Here is the communication flow and architecture:
â 
AI
<->
MCP Server
<->
Command Proxy Server
<->
Photoshop / Premiere UXP Plugin
<->
Photoshop / Premiere
The proxy server is required because UXP-based JavaScript plugins in Adobe apps can’t listen for incoming socket connections. They can only initiate outgoing ones as a client.
Using it is as simple as setting it up, and then telling the AI to do something in Photoshop.
Examples
Here is a list of some examples / experiments:
AI Agent for Photoshop / Rename Layers
AI Agent for Adobe Premiere / Photoshop: Create Photo Slideshow
AI Agent for Adobe Photoshop (MCP) : Create Instagram post
AI Agent for Adobe Premiere : Create Music Video From Random Clips
AI Agent for Adobe Photoshop (MCP) : Clean up layers
AI Agent for Adobe Photoshop (MCP) : User Driven
AI Agent for Adobe Photoshop (MCP) : Create a custom tutorial
AI Agent for Photoshop / Describe Content in Photoshop File
AI Agent for Premiere Pro / Create Sequences Based on Creation Date
All of these can by found in this YouTube playlist:
https://youtu.be/5p7oCdTVssk?si=SyI4kmmgJdT2P2dp
Areas for Improvement
This is a proof of concept project, and while it can actually be useful, there is a TON of room for improvement.
Not Production Ready
While the actual functionality and control works surprisingly well, it can be difficult to get setup, and requires some knowledge of working with the command line.
If Adobe were ever to release something like this, they would need to solve for bridging between the MCP and UXP plugins, which they could do in a couple of ways, including:
Including their own proxy server as part of Creative Cloud desktop
Building MCP support directly into the apps or Creative Cloud Desktop
Adding support for UXP plugins to listen on a socket connection (right now can only connect to a socket, not open one)
Passing Images
Currently, to pass images between the app, MCP server and AI, they are written to the filesystem. At least for Photoshop, it should be possible to pass everything directly through the socket.
AI Vision
As it is implemented right now, itâs not possible to get the app outpu

data.title: A year of funded FreeBSD development
data.author: cperciva
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FreeBSD操作系统的发展现状、驱动支持、企业资助情况及其在Unix生态中的定位。

不同观点：
• msdrigg分享了FreeBSD在2024年初启动过程变慢的问题，并通过提交历史追踪到根磁盘大小增加的提交。他通过将磁盘大小增加到8 GB恢复了性能，但其根本原因不明。
• AndyKelley强调了FreeBSD在Zig语言项目中的新支持，包括自动构建和跨平台编译功能，鼓励更多项目支持FreeBSD。
• net01提到BSD基金会在笔记本电脑项目上的投入，特别是实现S0ix睡眠状态等功能。
• tiffanyh对cperciva同时管理Tarsnap和FreeBSD工作表示钦佩。
• ksec批评亚马逊、谷歌、苹果和Meta等大公司对FreeBSD的支持不足，尽管这些公司从开源软件中获益，但 sponsorship 贡献较少。
• xedrac尝试用FreeBSD作为家庭网关服务器，但由于10 GbE网卡缺少驱动，最终选择了Nix。
• nithssh提到FreeBSD曾对Atheros WiFi卡的支持优于Linux，但现代混合CPU架构下调度器表现不佳。
• commandersaki好奇EC2上FreeBSD的主要用户是谁。
• johnnyjeans询问FreeBSD在Unix领域的独特定位，为什么不选择OpenBSD、NetBSD或Linux。
• LAC-Tech认为FreeBSD的开发状况令人担忧，操作系统复杂性需要全职的发布经理，而不仅仅是一年的兼职支持。

补充讨论：
• SSLy提到了一个编码问题，虽然没有详细说明。
• 讨论中多次提及企业资助问题，特别是大公司对开源项目的贡献不平衡，成为争议焦点。
• 不同用户对FreeBSD的驱动支持和在现代硬件上的表现有不同看法，特别是与Linux和其他BSD变种的比较。
• FreeBSD在特定技术（如ZFS、Nvidia驱动、ELF等）上的支持被认为是其在Unix领域中的优势，但也有人质疑其相对于Linux的独特性。

data.title: United States Digital Service Origins
data.author: ronbenton
data.article_summary: 《美国数字服务起源》是一份口述历史，记录了美国数字服务（United States Digital Service）的创立过程及其早期发展。该项目通过近50次访谈，涵盖2009至2015年，涉及创始成员及初期领导团队，展示了技术在政府中作用的愿景及其实现的挑战。关键主题和时间线揭示了该机构从概念到成立的过程，并提供了实际工作体验和不同视角的反思。这份口述历史不仅是关于美国数字服务本身，也属于更广泛的公民技术运动的一部分，强调了经验丰富的技术专家在政府中可以改善公共服务。尽管该服务在2025年经历了重组和更名，但其遗产和经验仍对未来政府技术团队具有重要意义。

• [历史背景与感谢] **mlinhares** 对参与者表示赞扬，认为他们的工作对国家产生了重大影响，并将被铭记。

44204277.article_content:
United States Digital Service Origins
An oral history documenting how the United States Digital Service came to exist, and the initial days of building its foundation.
Sign up for updates
June 6, 2025
Launching an Oral History of the Origins of the United States Digital Service
Opinions about technology’s role in government are everywhere right now. As founding members of the United States Digital Service, we could easily add our voices to the noise — especially after it was reorganized and renamed to the United States DOGE Service on January 20, 2025.
While there’s certainly a need to think strategically about the future, it is also critical that we understand and learn from the past, because hard-won lessons shouldn’t be overshadowed by controversy or politics. After all, having a government that functions and delivers on its promises to the public shouldn’t be divisive.
That’s why over the past several years we have been collecting stories and experiences from our colleagues — the people who laid the foundation for an organization that brought over 700 technologists into government across three presidential administrations. Today we are proud to share the outcome of this work:
an oral history documenting how the United States Digital Service came to exist, and the initial days of building its foundation.
The United States Digital Service Origins
features nearly 50 interviews, spanning 2009 – 2015, with those involved in the founding of the United States Digital Service, as well as some of the first leaders of agency teams and Communities of Practice. Each interview stands on its own, but in the aggregate the interviews piece together a larger story and vision of technology in government, and the realities of creating something new in an environment that is often paralyzed by inertia.
When we looked across interviews, we were able to identify
key themes and lessons
, and create a
chronology of events
that tell the story of how the U.S. Digital Service was conceptualized and how it came to life. We also identified
key quotes
that together provide a sense of the experience itself — what the work was actually like, as well as differing views and reflections on that time.
This is just one part of a larger story that led to the U.S. Digital Service; it’s one part of a 20+ year civic tech movement that transcends organizations, disciplines, and borders, and is built on the belief that people with experience designing and delivering digital products, combined with institutional knowledge and positioned at the right level of government, can transform public services — and that if we do this right, maybe we can make life even just a little bit better for people.
That story and movement doesn’t halt when one program — or presidency — comes to an end. Because it’s a body of work that’s bigger than any agency or group of people.
Whatever form government technology teams take in the coming years, the U.S. Digital Service’s legacy and learnings are relevant. It was not perfect, but it demonstrated what was possible, and those who had an opportunity to serve were forever changed.
– Kathy Pham and Emily Tavoulareas

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个AI工具（可能与AI生成动画或游戏素材相关）的评论，涵盖功能、质量、技术实现、使用体验以及对该工具真诚性的质疑。

不同观点：
• 正面观点：一些用户对该工具表示赞赏，认为它有潜力帮助独立开发者和动画师简化工作流程，特别是在处理动画中间帧等繁琐工作上（[bitwize]）。有用户表示期待该工具的未来发展，并希望了解其在特定游戏视角（如等距和俯视图）上的表现（[imatworkyo]）。

• 负面观点：部分用户对工具的质量和效果提出批评，认为生成的素材质量低且具有明显的AI“模糊感”，无法与人工设计相媲美（[9283409232]）。此外，有用户指出该工具可能只是借AI概念吸引关注和金钱，实际上没有提供太多创新或高质量的结果（[Madmallard]）。

• 技术问题与体验：许多用户报告了使用过程中的技术问题，如支付后积分未到账（[bigcat12345678]）、页面无响应（[ofjcihen]）、示例图片无法加载（[educasean]）以及操作30分钟未能达到预期效果（[banner520]）。还有用户提到设置和个人资料页面无法正常工作（[DrSiemer]）。

• 工具实现与开源质疑：有用户质疑该工具是否使用了开源模型和工具，并指出在FAQ中未找到相关信息（[elpocko]）。此外，有用户对该工具是否真正训练了自己的模型表示怀疑（[elpocko]）。

• 创意与道德问题：有用户担心AI生成工具会导致大量低质量游戏的产生，并可能抄袭人类艺术家的作品（[highway900]）。此外，有用户认为AI艺术工具不被视为真诚的艺术创作，建议开发者将重点放在艺术创作上，并考虑免费或开源以增加真诚性（[doctorpangloss]）。

补充讨论：
• 用户对AI生成动画在游戏开发中的实际应用表示关注，特别是对于复杂或创新项目的适用性存在疑虑（[iandanforth], [Madmallard]）。
• 有用户提到当前16x16像素级别AI生成素材的质量普遍不高，显示该领域仍有待改进（[mclau157]）。
• 一些用户对工具的定价和收费模式表示不满，认为类似工具已有很多免费选项，该工具可能只是借AI概念谋利（[Madmallard]）。

data.author: amrrs
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLMs）及语言模型推理能力（LRMs）的局限性与潜力

不同观点：
• **对LLMs能力的困惑与思考**：[throwaway71271] 认为LLMs使用语言的方式让人类感到困惑，尽管理解其内部机制，但其能力仍然像魔法一样难以捉摸。他强调需要更多努力去理解如何利用这些模型并构建更强大的系统。
• **复杂性与经济价值的关系**：[curious_cat_163] 对将复杂性映射到经济价值的讨论感兴趣，认为需要超越 puzzle 环境的评估方式，但仍需保持任务复杂性的可控性。
• **对AI发展的批评与怀疑**：[jbentley1] 质疑Apple在AI研发方面的投入，暗示其可能在忽视AI的重要性。[actinium226] 提到了AI发展中的"Gartner hype cycle"，暗示对AGI即将到来的过度期待。
• **LLMs与传统计算方法的结合**：[teleforce] 认为LLMs/LRMs在精确计算方面有局限，建议结合逻辑、优化和约束编程等方法来提升其能力。
• **LLMs在不同任务中的表现**：[thomasahle] 指出LLMs在允许编写代码的情况下可以完美解决某些任务，质疑研究中对LLMs能力的限制是否合理。[JusticeJuice] 对LLMs在不同复杂任务中的表现研究结果表示认可。
• **LLMs的思考模式与改进方向**：[cdrini] 认为当前LLMs在处理复杂问题时需要像人类一样能够在思考过程中进行迭代和修改，而不是一次性输出结果。[benlivengood] 强调持续进步，认为前言LLMs在性能上远超旧模型。
• **对研究定义的质疑**：[nialv7] 对研究中未明确定义“推理”、“可泛化性”和“模式匹配”等概念表示不满，认为需要先明确这些定义才能更好地理解研究结果。
• **对研究结果的解释**：[danck] 认为LLMs在复杂任务中失败是因为token预算不足，只要扩大token预算就能提高其能力。
• **对LLMs局限性的接受**：[esafak] 认为LLMs和人类一样有局限性，指出即使是人类也没有解决许多开放性问题。
• **对LLMs过度工程化的担忧**：[beneboy] 提到Claude在寻找正确解决方案时可能会过度工程化，研究结果揭示了这一问题。

补充讨论：
• **对AGI未来发展的讨论**：[antics] 认为当前模型是“全知却愚钝”的，并质疑这种状态是否会持续下去，认为需要更尖锐的分析来推动不同观点之间的对话。
• **历史视角与AI研发的经济驱动**：[d4rkn0d3z] 从历史角度回顾AI发展，指出当前AI研究更多受到资本驱动，而非科学探索，强调解决硬问题的重要性。

争议焦点：
• **LLMs是否具备真正的推理能力**：一些评论质疑LLMs是否能够进行真正的推理，还是仅仅依赖模式匹配。[nialv7] 强调需要明确定义和人类推理的对比。
• **LLMs在复杂任务中的表现是否可以通过简单扩展解决**：[danck] 认为通过增加token预算可以解决复杂任务中的问题，而[cdrini] 认为需要更类似于人类的思考和迭代过程。

总结：讨论围绕LLMs和LRMs的能力与局限性展开，涉及其在不同任务中的表现、改进方向以及与传统计算方法的结合。同时，对AI发展中的经济驱动和AGI未来发展的讨论也占据一定篇幅。

• **LLMs在不同任务中的表现**：[thomasahle] 指出LLMs在允许编写代码的情况下可以完美解决某些任务，质疑研究中对LLMs能力的限制是否合理。[JusticeJuice] 对LLMs在不同复杂任务中的表现研究结果表示认可。
• **LLMs的思考模式与改进方向**：[cdrini] 认为当前LLMs在处理复杂问题时需要像人类一样能够在思考过程中进行迭代和修改，而不是一次性输出结果。[benlivengood] 强调持续进步，认为前言LLMs在性能上远超旧模型。
• **对研究定义的质疑**：[nialv7] 对研究中未明确定义“推理”、“可泛化性”和“模式匹配”等概念表示不满，认为需要先明确这些定义才能更好地理解研究结果。
• **对研究结果的解释**：[danck] 认为LLMs在复杂任务中失败是因为token预算不足，只要扩大token预算就能提高其能力。
• **对LLMs局限性的接受**：[esafak] 认为LLMs和人类一样有局限性，指出即使是人类也没有解决许多开放性问题。
• **对LLMs过度工程化的担忧**：[beneboy] 提到Claude在寻找正确解决方案时可能会过度工程化，研究结果揭示了这一问题。

补充讨论：
• **对AGI未来发展的讨论**：[antics] 认为当前模型是“全知却愚钝”的，并质疑这种状态是否会持续下去，认为需要更尖锐的分析来推动不同观点之间的对话。
• **历史视角与AI研发的经济驱动**：[d4rkn0d3z] 从历史角度回顾AI发展，指出当前AI研究更多受到资本驱动，而非科学探索，强调解决硬问题的重要性。

争议焦点：
• **LLMs是否具备真正的推理能力**：一些评论质疑LLMs是否能够进行真正的推理，还是仅仅依赖模式匹配。[nialv7] 强调需要明确定义和人类推理的对比。
• **LLMs在复杂任务中的表现是否可以通过简单扩展解决**：[danck] 认为通过增加token预算可以解决复杂任务中的问题，而[cdrini] 认为需要更类似于人类的思考和迭代过程。

总结：讨论围绕LLMs和LRMs的能力与局限性展开，涉及其在不同任务中的表现、改进方向以及与传统计算方法的结合。同时，对AI发展中的经济驱动和AGI未来发展的讨论也占据一定篇幅。

主要讨论点：围绕核聚变研究进展及其未来潜力的不同观点和讨论。

不同观点：
• [支持与乐观]  
  - [ChuckMcM] 对核聚变工程进展持乐观态度，赞赏研究团队不断实现工程目标，并对未来五年内建成能源生产型仿星器（stellarator）充满信心。
  - [mrbluecoat] 赞赏科学成就和工程美学，感叹真空容器内部结构的复杂工程。

• [实用主义与怀疑态度]  
  - [Synaesthesia] 对核聚变持怀疑态度，认为应该更多关注核裂变和可再生能源（如太阳能和风能），并指出中国和俄罗斯在核能领域的领先地位。

• [技术实现与理论模型的讨论]  
  - [ninetyninenine] 质疑为何数学建模和模拟尚未提供完美的设计，并询问是否缺乏有效的数学模型，认为需要实际建造和测试才能验证设计。

• [对不同核聚变技术的比较与预测]  
  - [jablongo] 对未来十年内不同核聚变技术的成功可能性进行排名，认为仿星器可能在2060年成为主流设计，但在近期内更看好托卡马克和Helion的设计。

补充讨论：
• [对具体技术指标的解释]  
  - [Robotbeat] 强调核聚变研究中的关键指标——等离子体“三重积”，并解释了Lawson准则及其在不同核聚变方法比较中的应用。

• [提供信息来源]  
  - [_Microft] 提供官方网站声明以支持讨论。
  - [s1artibartfast] 提供存档和替代信息来源以供参考。

• [对人工智能与核聚变进展的类比]  
  - [ipnon] 将人工智能的发展轨迹与核聚变进行类比，认为两者都存在预期与现实的差距。

争议焦点：
• 核聚变技术是否能在短期内实现实际应用，还是应该更多地关注其他能源解决方案。  
• 数学建模和模拟在核聚变设计中的局限性以及实际建造和测试的必要性。

data.title: A Rippling Townhouse Facade by Alex Chinneck Takes a Seat in a London Square
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 英国艺术家Alex Chinneck在伦敦Clerkenwell设计周上展出了新作《A week at the knees》。这件雕塑位于 Charterhouse Square，重塑了一栋经典乔治亚风格联排别墅的外墙，使其下两层仿佛波浪般“坐”在路径上，给人一种轻盈、玩味的视觉效果。雕塑高5米，重12吨，由320米再生钢和7,000块砖制成，厚度仅15厘米，呈现出厚重建筑结构与轻盈姿态的对比。该作品与多家英国公司合作完成，结合了定制的钢梁、弯曲的窗户和砖块，并在细节上融入了周围历史环境的元素，如排水管和拱门前门两侧的灯具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[对某个建筑或雕塑作品的不同看法，包括其与自然的关系、工艺难度以及对作品的感受]

不同观点：
• [impossiblefork] 认为该建筑（或雕塑）虽然是有趣的，但觉得砖结构是对自然的一种人为强加，更喜欢原本生长在那里的草木。他觉得如果这是一个隧道可能会更好。
• [hn_throwaway_99] 对作品的工艺表示赞赏，特别是窗户的部分。他认为在曲面上制作和安装弯曲的窗框和窗格非常困难，而作品中实现了这一点显示出对细节的极致关注，增加了整体的 illusion 效果，使其看起来像一块可折叠的地毯。
• [adammarples] 没有表达对作品的具体看法，只是询问作品的位置，显示出对作品背景信息的兴趣。
• [egypturnash] 以轻松的语气表示想要玩一个与此作品相关的滑板游戏，表现出对作品的娱乐性联想。
• [readthenotes1] 对作品的经济成本提出质疑，使用“More money than sense”这一短语来表达对资源投入的怀疑，并通过文字游戏（“pense”代替“sense”）增加评论的幽默感。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点可能在于作品是否与自然和谐共存。impossiblefork 认为这是对自然的人为干预，而其他评论没有直接回应这一观点，更多关注作品的工艺和娱乐价值。
• hn_throwaway_99 对工艺细节的分析提供了技术性的视角，强调了作品在设计和执行上的难度和精细程度。
• 其他评论如 adammparples 和 egypturnash 更多的是对作品的个人兴趣和娱乐联想，没有涉及深层次的批评或分析。
• readthenotes1 的评论带有幽默性质，对作品的经济性提出质疑，但没有深入展开。

总体而言，评论中既有对作品美学和工艺的欣赏，也有对其与自然关系的批评，还有对作品背景和娱乐性的好奇。

44203870.article_content:
Photos by Charles Emerson. All images courtesy of Alex Chinneck Studio, shared with permission
A Rippling Townhouse Facade by Alex Chinneck Takes a Seat in a London Square
May 22, 2025
Art
Design
Kate Mothes
Share
Pin
Email
Bookmark
It takes a real knack for design to make something as hefty and industrial as steel and bricks appear weightless or even playful. But British artist
Alex Chinneck
(
previously
) is no stranger to monumental projects that reimagine urban infrastructure and buildings into striking public installations.
As part of London’s
Clerkenwell Design Week
, Chinneck unveiled “A week at the knees,” a new sculpture in Charterhouse Square that takes its cue from
an iconic predecessor
. The artist installed the “From the Knees of my Nose to the Belly of my Toes” in 2013 on a dilapidated townhouse in Margate, appearing as though the entire front of the building had simply slid right off. On view through June in London, his new work boasts a frame made from 320 meters of repurposed steel and 7,000 bricks.
“A week at the knees” playfully anthropomorphizes a classic Georgian facade, with its lower two levels rippling over a pathway as if seated in the park with its knees up. London is famous for its green squares and gardens, and Chinneck’s work invites visitors to pass through a unique portal that calls upon the history of its surroundings, complete with downspout and lamps flanking the arched front door.
Chinneck fabricated the sculpture in collaboration with numerous British companies to source and create bespoke steel beams, curving windows, and bricks. At five meters tall and weighing 12 tons, the piece mimics a life-size building while sporting a thickness of only 15 centimeters. The effect lends itself to the experience of a hefty, architectonic structure with a graceful, lightweight personality.

website
and

.

data.title: SaaS is just vendor lock-in with better branding
data.author: pistoriusp
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了SaaS服务带来的隐性成本，尽管它们声称能帮助开发者专注于产品开发。实际上，集成第三方服务（如认证、文件存储等）会产生五种“隐性税收”：

1. **发现税**：需要研究服务是否适合你的技术栈及其定价。
2. **注册税**：提供个人信息和支付方式，可能面临定价 tier 锁定和额外费用。
3. **集成税**：实际操作中需要处理文档未提及的边缘情况，增加工作量。
4. **本地开发税**：确保服务在本地运行，可能需要云端隧道，增加配置复杂性。
5. **生产税**：在生产环境中管理服务的可靠性，包括API密钥管理和监控。

文章建议选择集成平台（如Cloudflare或Supabase）来避免这些隐性成本，因为它们提供统一的服务环境，减少了上下文切换和兼容性问题，提高了开发流畅性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SaaS（软件即服务）的优缺点，尤其是关于供应商锁定（vendor lock-in）和成本效益的讨论。

不同观点：
• [foundart] 认为SaaS在公司早期能帮助控制成本，但随着公司规模扩大，SaaS可能导致供应商锁定问题，最终使客户得不偿失。SaaS的问题是成功后的负面副作用。
• [lokimedes] 将SaaS视为现代版的“寻租”行为，认为这是反社会经济学的，应被抵制和定为非法。同时，他也认为免费软件经济上也不理想，因为它不能充分回报创作者的努力。他建议将软件购买与服务协议分开。
• [pjmlp] 指出SaaS是让开发者为工具付费的解决方案，类似于其他专业人士为工具付费。如果不喜欢SaaS，应该通过支持上游开发者来改变。
• [jgord] 将供应商锁定与宗教类比，认为如果有标准格式数据且能轻松迁移，就不算真正的锁定。许多SaaS平台不允许客户轻松访问其数据，导致客户更易感到不满。
• [citizenpaul] 强调长期合同导致的深度锁定问题，比如与Oracle/MS/IBM/Salesforce的多年合同，使得公司难以更换平台。
• [0xbadcafebee] 认为所有选择都存在某种锁定，但真正的锁定是难以替换或替换成本极高的选择。主张选择支持业务灵活性的解决方案，而不是因为“反正都会锁定”而选择某个平台。

补充讨论：
• [AstroBen] 质疑通过加深锁定来对抗锁定的逻辑。
• [solatic] 认为原文实际是反对与过多供应商打交道，而不是反对SaaS本身，主张减少供应商和依赖以简化生活。
• [abelanger] 认为开放源代码和自托管能解决许多锁定的“税”（如发现、注册、集成和本地开发），开放源代码能缓解这些问题。
• [paxys] 认为供应商锁定在某些情况下是天赐之物，特别是在技术环境不稳定时，使用稳定的大公司技术如AWS可以避免频繁迁移技术。
• [missedthecue] 指出SaaS的吸引力在于其年金式收入和定价权。
• [gavmor] 将发现和比较SaaS服务的成本视为O(n log n)问题，搜索和比较是现代技术混乱的一部分。
• [davidpaulyoung] 主张使用可选择自托管的开源SaaS。
• [nitwit005] 担心供应商在几年后大幅提高价格，特别是在产品销量下降时。
• [klysm] 强调供应商锁定的核心问题是供应商对定价的控制权。

争议焦点：SaaS是否导致不可接受的供应商锁定以及其长期成本效益。一些人认为SaaS早期有益，但成功后可能成为问题，而另一些人则认为开放源代码和自托管是更好的解决方案。

SaaS Is Just Vendor Lock-In with Better Branding
Developers are told "to focus on the product" and let SaaS vendors handle the rest, but integrating third-party services, whether it's auth, queuing, file storage, or image optimization, comes at a cost. Not just in dollars but in time, friction, and mental overhead.
There are five hidden taxes you pay every time you integrate a SaaS into your stack.
1. The Discovery Tax
Before you can integrate anything, you first have to figure out what they're actually selling?
What problems are they solving?
Is it compatible with your stack?
Is their price sane at your scale? a
Are their docs clear and do they reveal any implementation weirdness?
This unpaid research work is usually non-transferable. What you learn about "Uploady" or "MegaQueue" doesn't help you next time when you're evaluating something else. It's also subjective. It's marketing, and does the marketing message resonate with you?
2. The Sign-Up Tax
You've decided on a service, and this is the moment when you hand over your email and credit card.
Do they support usage-based pricing or only lock-in tiers?
Can your team members access the dashboard, or do you have to pay more for that functionality? Despite only using the service the same amount!
Can you even test the product without hitting a paywall?
You're now on the hook, even if you haven't written a single line of code.
3. The Integration Tax
Now the real work begins.
You read the docs.
You install the libraries
You wire it into your framework.
And figure out the edge cases that the docs don't mention, because docs are marketing!
Often you're left fighting your own tooling. They're aiming for the lowest common denominator, and you're bleeding edge. Or the other way around!
4. The Local Development Tax
You need the SaaS service to work locally. Does it even offer a local emulator? Can you stub it out in tests? Do you need to tunnel to the cloud just to test one feature?
Now you've got branching configuration logic, one for production, one for staging, one for local… If you're lucky.
5. The Production Tax
This is the part where you're "done," except you're not.
Can you use this in your staging environment? What about pull request previews?
You need to securely manage the API keys.
Monitoring, logging, and alerting
Wondering why something worked in your laptop but fails in production?
You've integrated the service, but now you're on the hook for its reliability in production.
Conclusion
The pitch of modern SaaS is "don't reinvent the wheel." But every wheel you bolt on comes with some friction. It's not just a service: It's a contract. It's a dependency. It's a subtle architectural shift, and it comes with taxes.
No matter what choice you make, it's always going to be vendor-locked in. Switching out something, even if it's open source and self-hosted, means that you're rewriting a lot of code.
So, my argument is, don't make those decisions. Just pick a platform. The thing that matters is the software that you want to write, not the framework or the services that it runs on.
Platforms like Cloudflare or Supabase shine. Where your database, queue, image service, and storage all live within the same platform and speak the same language. You avoid paying these taxes repeatedly. You simply pick the product that's already there.
No context switching between vendors.
No API key wrangling.
No compatibility hacks or configuration forks.
Just fast, local feeling integrations that work the same in dev and production.
It feels like everything is running on the same machine, and in a way it kind of is. That's the hidden superpower of integrated platforms. They collapse the distance between your code and your services. And in doing so, they give you back the one thing no SaaS vendor can sell you: "Flow."

文章主要讨论了SaaS服务带来的隐性成本，尽管它们声称能帮助开发者专注于产品开发。实际上，集成第三方服务（如认证、文件存储等）会产生五种“隐性税收”：

1. **发现税**：需要研究服务是否适合你的技术栈及其定价。
2. **注册税**：提供个人信息和支付方式，可能面临定价 tier 锁定和额外费用。
3. **集成税**：实际操作中需要处理文档未提及的边缘情况，增加工作量。
4. **本地开发税**：确保服务在本地运行，可能需要云端隧道，增加配置复杂性。
5. **生产税**：在生产环境中管理服务的可靠性，包括API密钥管理和监控。

文章建议选择集成平台（如Cloudflare或Supabase）来避免这些隐性成本，因为它们提供统一的服务环境，减少了上下文切换和兼容性问题，提高了开发流畅性。

• [missedthecue] 指出SaaS的吸引力在于其年金式收入和定价权。

• [nitwit005] 担心供应商在几年后大幅提高价格，特别是在产品销量下降时。
• [klysm] 强调供应商锁定的核心问题是供应商对定价的控制权。

data.author: cmogni1
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了为何在批量任务中，开源大型语言模型（LLM）比闭源模型更具优势。尽管在高端智能任务中，闭源模型如GPT、Claude和Gemini仍占主导地位，但对于许多常见业务任务（如文本分类、摘要、数据提取等），开源模型表现同样出色，且成本更低。文章比较了开源和闭源模型的性能和成本，指出对于“工作马”模型（workhorse models），开源模型提供了更高的性价比，尤其是在使用批量推理服务时，能实现显著的成本节约。文章还介绍了如何使用人工智能指数（Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index）来评估模型性能，并提供了开源替代模型的推荐及相应的成本节约预期。

Workhorse LLMs: Why Open Source Models Dominate Closed Source for Batch Tasks
Sutro Team
Jun 6, 2025
As LLMs become more prolific, weâve noticed that teams still reach for closed sourced models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini for nearly every task. While this may have been the right call a year ago, teams today are unknowingly missing out on huge cost savings and performance gains by not considering open source alternatives.
It is true that at the frontier of intelligence, the most powerful closed source LLMs dominate their open source counterparts. However, many common tasks for LLMs donât require PhD level reasoning. Instead, they require a workhorse LLM: something thatâs reliable for low-to-medium difficulty tasks â things like classification, summarization, and data extraction.
Not only are there suitable replacements for closed source workhorses like GPT-4o-mini, but the equivalent replacements are often less expensive
and
more intelligent. When latency isnât an issue, open source models have an even larger edge for cost savings if running jobs in bulk through a batch inference provider like Sutro.
In this guide, we compare the performance and cost of workhorse models. After the analysis, we provide a handy conversion chart that helps you pick the best open source replacement for the closed source models you may have used along with the cost savings you should expect by making the switch.
How Do Open Source LLMs Stack Up Against Closed Source LLMs?
A common question organizations ask us is how the cost and performance of open source models stack up against closed source models. To answer this question, itâs best to divide the field into two categories: frontier models and workhorse models.
Frontier models are the biggest, most capable models. They promise emergent capabilities, generalization across tasks, and the ability to handle complex context and instructions.
At the frontier, closed source models like Claude Opus 4.0, OpenAIâs o3 model, and Gemini 2.5 Pro dominate. However, open source models like Qwen 3 235B-A22B and DeepSeek R1 (and the to-be-released R2) are closing the gap quickly.
The closed providers also provide smaller, less-expensive models. These include GPT-4o mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Haiku 3.5. Many companies choose to adopt these models to save on costs when running tasks that require less general reasoning capabilities.  We refer to these as âworkhorseâ models, and believe that for this class of model open-source dominates.
Workhorse models are extremely adept at most common business tasks, including:
Structured Extraction:
Turning free form-text or images into JSON format and analytics-ready datasets.
Summarizing Text:
Turning large documents or conversations into bullet points or summaries.
Answering Questions:
Doing Q&A that doesnât require complex reasoning on your documents.
Sentiment Analysis:
Determining how positive, negative, or neutral a given text is.
Generating Synthetic Data:
Creating datasets from scratch to power fine-tuning or improving RAG systems.
Data Extraction And Organization:
Finding and extracting particular pieces of information from unstructured text.
Classification:
Sorting text into categories specific to your applications.
Running Evals:
Evaluating the robustness of your prompts using techniques like LLM-as-a-judge and metric scoring.
Most organizations already use models like GPT-4o-mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash to do these tasks to speed up inference and keep costs low. As we demonstrate below, equivalent open source LLMs can get you the same or better performance, sometimes with huge cost savings, especially if using a batch API like Sutro.
How Open Source LLMs For Common Business Tasks Stack Up
Figuring out how well an LLM performs is tricky. Most model creators game benchmarks by training for the test and testing using prompts that are carefully crafted to perform well. Nonetheless, because model providers are all trying to game the system in similar ways, benchmarks still give us a heuristic for
relative
capabilities.
To determine which workhorse open source models are likely a good replacement performance and cost wise for closed source models you have probably used, we will use Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index. The Intelligence Index is a weighted average of benchmarks across many tasks. Using this lets us not overweight any one benchmark and helps us get the heuristic we are looking for.
Additionally, we pulled together the average cost per token for common workhorse tasks. We used a 10:1 blended ratio of input-to-output tokens for non-thinking models, which we calculated from internal metrics. For models with thinking mode, we budgeted 2k thinking tokens, adjusting the blended ratio to 3:2.

不同观点：
• [taylodl] 认为，企业在使用公共道路时，不应以商业机密为由隐藏数据。公众有权知道自动驾驶车辆的安全记录，特斯拉试图阻止数据披露是反透明、反公共利益的行为。

• [jqpabc123] 支持透明度的立场，质疑特斯拉隐瞒安全记录的做法，并指出特斯拉 CEO 马斯克在消费者关系和信任建立方面表现不佳。该评论还暗示马斯克可能更适合从事政治和政府合同相关的工作，而非消费者领域。

• [diebeforei485] 则持不同意见，认为自动驾驶市场竞争激烈，特斯拉不应向竞争对手（如 Waymo）透露其策略和计划，尤其是在其他公司已经获得运营许可的情况下。

44205599.article_content:
The coin mold fragments found in Tadmekka, Mali.
Photograph by Clare Britt, Courtesy The Block Museum of Art
In This Story
Destination Guide
Mali
1 Articles
7 Places
When Sam Nixon, an archaeologist
with the British Museum, excavated ancient coin molds in Tadmekka, Mali, in 2005, it triggered a several-year exploration of how medieval Africans purified the gold they were using for their currency. Nixon had
found
little droplets of highly refined gold left over in the molds—which have been dated to the 11th century—as well as curious fragments of glass. Now scientists have recreated the advanced process behind the purification method they used then.
“This is the first time in the archaeological record that we saw glass being used to be able to refine gold,” says Marc Walton, codirector of the
Center for Scientific Studies in the Arts
, a collaboration between Northwestern University and the Art Institute of Chicago. “The glass appeared to be material that was [actually] recycled glass materials … so it really shows the industriousness and creativity of the craftsmen, who understood the properties of gold and glass enough to [use them for] this process of refining gold.” The recycled glass materials were remnants of broken vessels. Tadmekka was a town right in the middle of the trans-Saharan caravan route, so Nixon uncovered several types of material culture that had to do with trade, namely molds for “bald dinar,” or coins that hadn’t been stamped with the name of a mint (or a 10th-century equivalent of one).
An illuminated atlas depicts Mansa Musa, emperor of Mali from 1312 to 1337, widely known for his vast vast wealth in the form of gold deposits.
Courtesy The Block Museum of Art
According to Walton, Europeans in the 10th and 11th centuries purified their gold through cupellation, a process in which lead is mixed with gold laced with impurities, and then heated in a furnace until the droplets of purer gold can be skimmed off. But in the case of medieval West Africans, “They were taking the ore and other raw materials from the river and mixing it with glass,” says Walton. Since gold is inert, it doesn’t fully dissolve into melted glass, while impurities and other materials do, making this “a really novel way of using recycled glass material.”
Walton’s team at the Center for Scientific Studies in the Arts replicates a lot of ancient technologies. To get to the bottom of how medieval Africans purified gold so successfully, they also made do with what their environment provided them. “We bought gold dust from a chemical supply company and then we mixed it with local Lake Michigan sand and then we made our own synthetic glass,” says Walton. “We heated it up, were able to dissolve the minerals in the sand, and were left behind with gold.”
Though Walton and his team updated this small-scale, bespoke process for purifying gold to modern times and adapted it to their environment in Illinois, their results show that the medieval Malian technique was both clever and sophisticated.

And a description of some very stoned canines.

data.title: Highly efficient matrix transpose in Mojo
data.author: timmyd
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何使用Mojo语言在Hopper架构上实现高效的矩阵转置内核。该内核实现了2775.49 GB/s的带宽，性能接近CUDA的2771.35 GB/s。文章详细描述了实现步骤，包括初始化TMA描述符、加载数据到共享内存、执行转置计算、以及将结果存储回全局内存。

主要步骤如下：

1. **初始化TMA描述符**：创建两个描述符，分别对应原始矩阵和转置矩阵。
2. **加载到共享内存**：使用TMA将数据异步复制到共享内存。
3. **计算转置**：在共享内存中完成矩阵转置。
4. **存储到GMEM**：将转置结果存储回全局内存。
5. **Swizzling优化**：通过调整描述符和索引实现进一步优化。

文章还提到，Mojo通过使用PTX API实现了比CUDA更高的带宽。Swizzling技术也被提及，提供了相关代码示例和详细解释的链接。最终的内核在性能上媲美CUDA，展示了Mojo在GPU计算上的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Mojo编程语言及其在矩阵转置等操作中的应用和性能的讨论，包括其实用性、性能表现、以及是否适用于实际生产环境。

不同观点：
• daft_pink认为Mojo并不是一个真正的开放产品，其存在主要是为了推动Modular公司的利润，且在2025年使用授权编程语言是不切实际的。
• saagarjha分析了Mojo使用PTX API进行TMA传输的性能，认为虽然Mojo在某些情况下表现优于CUDA，但他不确定是否总是需要TMA来实现高速操作，尤其是在简单转置任务中。
• sestep质疑将矩阵转置与前后操作融合的效率，认为这种融合操作可能更常见且更高效。
• totalperspectiv关注粗粒度代码中的@parameter-for使用，询问这是否会导致代码体积增大，并表示从文章中学到了很多。
• londons_explore质疑是否有必要单独进行矩阵转置，建议将其与后续操作结合以提高效率。
• iandanforth对图形表示提出疑问，认为图形中的向量在最终矩阵中应按列排列。
• thunkingdeep指出“archive”可能应为“achieve”，质疑是否存在术语使用错误。
• melodyogonna好奇是否存在不使用Modular提供的高级抽象的理由。
• graycat提出快速矩阵转置可以通过改变索引算法实现，而不需要复杂的操作。
• arjvik质疑所谓14%的性能提升，认为实际提升仅为0.14%。
• vlan121强调Mojo编译器闭源是一个大问题。
• colesantiago询问是否有企业在生产环境中使用Mojo或招聘Mojo开发者。
• almostgotcaught赞同londons_explore的观点，认为不应单独编写转置内核，应融合其他操作。
• jsnell指出文章标题存在误导，实际性能提升仅为0.14%而非14%。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Mojo在矩阵转置任务中的实际性能提升是否如宣传所言，特别是0.14%与14%之间的差距。
• 另一个值得注意的点是Mojo编译器闭源问题及其对该语言广泛应用的影响。
• 讨论还涉及是否应将矩阵转置与其他操作结合以提高效率，以及高层次抽象和简单索引算法在矩阵操作中的应用。

data.title: Researchers develop ‘transparent paper’ as alternative to plastics
data.author: anigbrowl
data.article_summary: 日本研究团队开发出一种以植物纤维素为基础的透明纸张，作为塑料的替代品。这种纸张具有可生物降解性，能够在海洋环境中被微生物分解为水和二氧化碳。其制作过程使用棉籽纤维表面的纤维素粉末，溶解于溴化锂水溶液中并加热成胶状，然后成型和干燥。该材料厚度为0.7毫米时仍保持透明和柔韧，可用于制作杯子、吸管等容器，强度接近聚碳酸酯塑料。尽管生产成本是普通纸张的三倍，但二氧化碳排放量仅为塑料生产的一半。这种透明纸解决了传统纸包装无法展示内容物的问题，有望在市场上替代塑料包装。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：塑料替代品的可行性与环境影响

不同观点：
• fastball认为，当前使用塑料的原因在于其轻便和耐用性，而不是透明度。他强调塑料在人类生活条件下的持久性是一个优点，并提出需要开发一种在常见条件下不易降解、但在特定触发条件下可快速降解的材料。
• kazinator和wolfi1提到历史上存在的类似材料，如赛璐珞和玻璃纸，暗示这些材料可能是现代塑料的替代品。
• pupppet批评一些国家将垃圾倾倒进海洋，而不是解决这一问题，反而在制造更好的垃圾，暗示对现有废物处理系统的不满。
• Huxley1分享了其实际经验，提到在尝试减少塑料包装时遇到成本和材料耐用性的问题，并对透明纸材料（如纤维素材料）表示兴趣，希望了解其实际使用效果。
• speedylight主张开发具有塑料特性但降解速度更快或易于回收的新材料。
• smolder认为石油衍生材料应优先用于替代困难的领域，如医学，而不是能源消耗，主张保留石油用于对人类有重大贡献的用途。
• 1970-01-01对环保产品中的某些具体应用（如吸管）持怀疑态度，认为并非所有环保产品设计都是完美的。
• bosky101对透明纸材料的研发表示支持和兴奋。
• JBlue42基于在日本的观察，批评日本过度使用塑料包装，表达了对该问题的不满。
• giantg2怀疑透明纸材料的化学处理是否比塑料更环保，暗示材料替代可能只是形式上的改变而非实质上的环保。
• ekianjo批评日本过度包装文化，认为在推广透明纸材料前应先解决包装浪费问题。

补充讨论：
• JumpCrisscross对透明纸纤维的排列方式表示技术兴趣，关注材料科学的具体实现。
• 总体讨论中，争议的焦点在于塑料替代品的实际可行性和环境效益，特别是成本、材料性能和文化习惯对环境的影响。

44205282.article_content:
Technology
Japanese Researchers Develop ‘Transparent Paper’ as Alternative to Plastics; New Material Is Biodegradable, Can Be Produced with Low Carbon Emissions
Post
Share
Post
Photos courtesy of JAMSTEC
Scenery 100 meters away is seen through a sheet of transparent paper which is 0.7 millimeters thick.
The Yomiuri Shimbun
14:47 JST, June 5, 2025
A team of researchers with the Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology (JAMSTEC) and other entities have developed thick sheets of transparent paper using cellulose, a material made from plant biomass.
The transparent paper sheets can be broken down by microbes into water and carbon dioxide. Also, they can be used to make containers because they are thicker than conventional cellulose-based materials. The new material is expected to replace plastics for this purpose, as plastics are a source of ocean pollution.
To make the paper sheets, the team used cellulose powder made from fibers found on the surfaces of cotton seeds. They dissolved the powder in a lithium bromide-water solution, mixing it in as they raised it to a high temperature until it became a gel, at which point the material was shaped and dried.
When the researchers shaped the material into cups and straws, they found that it was about as strong as polycarbonate, a type of plastic.
The paper sheets become transparent because they are packed tightly with nanometer-scale (one 1-billionth of a meter) fibers. The concentration of these fibers allows light to pass straight through the sheets without experiencing diffusion.
Even a sheet of the transparent paper that is 0.7 millimeters thick remains flexible, and scenery 100 meters away can be clearly seen through it.
On the assumption that the paper sheets will be washed into the ocean, the team investigated its biodegradability. The researchers sank the paper sheets into the ocean and checked whether microbes there were able to dissolve them.
The results showed that the deeper the place under the sea was, the slower the dissolution progressed, because there are fewer microbes in the deep ocean. But the paper sheets were mostly dissolved within four months even at 757 meters below the surface.
Photos courtesy of JAMSTEC
A cup and a straw made of the newly developed transparent paper
So far, paper packs have been the most common alternatives to plastic containers.
But business experts have pointed out that consumers are less willing to buy goods in paper packs because they cannot see the contents.
Transparent paper could overcome this problem, but bringing the material to market will require factories with the technology to mass-produce it.
Noriyuki Isobe, a deputy chief researcher for JAMSTEC, said, “If a plant for demonstration experiments of the technology is built, we estimate that the cost to produce the material will be about three times that of ordinary paper, while the volume of CO2 emissions can be kept to about half that of the plastic making process.”
Prof. Masaya Nogi of the University of Osaka, an expert on wooden materials, said, “There have been other types of transparent paper in the past, but the advantage of this over those is that it has been proven to be biodegradable in the deep sea.”

data.title: What “working” means in the era of AI apps
data.author: Brysonbw
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了人工智能（AI）时代下初创公司的快速增长现象。相比于前AI时代，AI驱动的企业能够在更短时间内实现更高的收入，并以更快的速度完成融资轮次。例如，企业级公司在第一年内的中位收入已超过200万美元，消费者公司在八个月内达到420万美元收入。此外，顶级公司与一般公司之间的差距在扩大，顶级公司能持续加速增长。尽管收入增长迅速，其他指标如用户参与度和留存率依然重要。消费者公司也逐渐成为真正的创收业务，特别是在新模型发布时会出现显著增长。总体而言，AI应用时代为软件公司创造了前所未有的发展机会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕AI应用对创业公司收入和成功的影响的讨论

不同观点：
• [nilirl] 认为文章标题有误导性，内容并未详细讨论AI应用对有偿工作的影响。文章声称LLM（大语言模型）提升了收入积累速度，但未解释LLM如何具体影响这些数据。文章暗示LLM提高发货速度和产品迭代速度，但未探讨其影响程度或提供反例。
• [ednite] 从外部视角出发，指出当前AI预期过于高涨，尤其是非技术人群中的 hype。虽然当前的AI工具比以往的技术（如Y2K或dot-com泡沫）更具实质性，但最终决定AI是否会改变世界的是其财务可行性，而非单纯的创新或炒作。
• [scubbo] 认为文章表明成功的最低标准大幅提高，而创业者需要具备在逆境中超越他人的信念。
• [nothrowaways] 对文章来源（a16z）持怀疑态度，尤其是因为其在加密货币热潮中的表现。
• [csomar] 指出AI的一个主要问题，即运营支出（OpEx）随着收入增长而增长，打破了传统应用工程中收入增长与利润增长的模式。同时提到，使用免费的高质量AI工具可能掩盖实际的运营成本。
• [babyshake] 对文章中“working”一词的使用感到困惑，原以为文章会讨论白领工作的变化，而不是筹资和增长策略。
• [JustinCS] 认为文章可能存在选择偏差，因为AI初创公司大多刚刚起步，成功者必然是快速增长的。未来的成功案例可能会有不同的增长轨迹。投资者现在期望更快见到收入，这对创始人和B2C应用更具吸引力。
• [hn_throwaway_99] 认为AI环境让创始人“更快失败”，员工也能更快获得信号，不必浪费时间。但这也让需要大量前期投资和时间的创意更难获得资金，这令人遗憾。
• [GiorgioG] 对当前AI hype持怀疑态度，表示需要五年后回头看才能验证其影响。
• [gerdesj] 将当前的AI热潮比作过去的郁金香热潮，暗示文章内容可能只是跟风炒作。
• [jvanderbot] 指出文章结论模糊，可能支持多种不同的结论，但缺乏足够的数据支持。
• [koakuma-chan] 质疑Cursor如何实现1亿收入，是否通过大幅加价实现。
• [yojo] 关注文章聚焦的收入指标，指出依赖第三方LLM API的初创公司可能面临更高的成本，这对其可持续性构成挑战。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI对创业公司收入和成功的实际影响，以及当前AI工具的运营成本和可持续性问题。
• 讨论中多次提到AI热潮的预期过高，以及对创新和财务可行性之间的平衡关注。
• 对文章结论和数据支持的质疑也是讨论的重要部分，尤其是不同读者对文章结论的多种解读。

What “Working” Means in the Era of AI Apps
Olivia Moore
and
Marc Andrusko

Table of Contents
Posted June 6, 2025
One of the most common refrains in the generative AI era is that “startups are growing faster than ever” — often with fewer resources. Some notable examples? Per company metrics, Lovable
hit
$50 million
in revenue in just six months, Cursor
reported
$100 million
in revenue in its first year, and Gamma
reached
$50 million
in revenue on less than $25 million raised.
But for the
average
AI company (not the top 0.1%), what does growth really look like? Pre-AI, a common benchmark for best-in-class enterprise startups was $1 million in ARR in its first 12 months. Consumer companies, by contrast, often delayed monetization well beyond their first year, typically waiting until they had built a base of millions (or tens of millions) of users to monetize through ads.
Based on data across hundreds of companies we’ve seen over the last 18 months, we can definitively say these metrics have shifted. Here’s what we’re seeing among the companies we’ve spent significant time with:
What does this mean for founders?
1. Faster revenue, faster rounds.
Our data backs up the idea that we’re in a new era of startup growth. The median enterprise company in our sample set reached more than $2 million in ARR in its first year, raising a Series A just nine months post-monetization. Median consumer companies performed even better, reaching $4.2 million in ARR and raising an A round within eight months. What was once considered “best in class” — the $0 to $1 million ARR ramp — is now on the lower end of growth we’re seeing.
Given the rapid growth both AI-native B2B and B2C companies are achieving between Seed and Series A, startups looking to raise venture capital need a strong velocity story. If not yet in live commercial traction, then certainly in shipping speed and product iteration. Speed is becoming a moat.
2. The gap between “good” and “exceptional” is growing.
While the bar has been raised across the board, top performers are really pulling away. Many of these breakout companies continue to pick up steam through their first year, rather than seeing growth start to slow (as we often saw in the pre-AI era). There’s demand from both enterprise and consumer users for great products, so it’s worth swinging for the fences.
It’s not just about revenue — other metrics still matter. When evaluating companies at the Series A stage, we often have no more than 12 months of usage and retention data. Later-stage financing rounds will likely rely more heavily on traditional software metrics; rapid top-line growth won’t be enough to compensate for low engagement or high churn.
3. Consumer companies are now…real (revenue-generating!) businesses.
Somewhat surprisingly, the revenue benchmarks for B2C are outpacing those for B2B. This is partially because consumer companies have a different “shape” now. One-third of the consumer companies in our sample raised significant funding to train their own models — and many see a massive revenue jump following new model releases. These spikes often resemble step function growth, which can later plateau until the next release.
While conversion to paid may be lower for generative AI B2C businesses compared to their pre-AI counterparts,
our data
suggests that once users
do
convert, they retain just as well.
*  *  *
TL;DR: Startups are working faster than ever, and both businesses and consumers are demonstrating high willingness to pay for new products. After combing through the data, we believe there’s never been a better time to build an application-layer software company.

data.title: Smalltalk, Haskell and Lisp
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者在用Haskell、Common Lisp和Smalltalk三种语言解决同一问题时的体验。作者发现，尽管Haskell不一定是最实用或最合适的选择，但其代码简洁、清晰，且具有高度的模块化，特别适合其编程风格。相比之下，Smalltalk和Lisp的实现尽管功能相似，但前者显得冗长，后者则因语法和宏的使用让作者感觉像是在“欺骗”语言来实现目标，而非直接表达意图。作者尤其欣赏Haskell的`where`语法，可以轻松地将复杂操作分解为简单部分，使代码更具可读性和表达力。总体而言，作者认为Haskell在代码美学和编程体验上优于Lisp和Smalltalk。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同编程语言的特性和编程风格的比较与讨论，包括Lisp、Haskell、Smalltalk等，以及对代码可读性和模块化设计的探讨。

不同观点：
• [neilv] 认为Lisp代码看起来不错，提供了一个函数定义示例，并解释了其功能。该评论者对Lisp的函数式风格持积极态度。
• [wk_end] 对Lisp的感情复杂，一方面欣赏其功能性风格和编译器支持，另一方面认为Lisp语言本身在当代并不十分有趣，且存在语言和库的混乱问题。但他也提到最近在业余时间使用Lisp编程感到非常愉快。
• [0x445442] 对文章中的Smalltalk实现表示不满，认为应通过发送消息给对象来实现功能，以提高可读性。
• [xelxebar] 提出了一个APL的解决方案，并对不同语言的实现方式表示了看法，认为核心结构类似，但具体实现依赖于对函数意义的猜测。
• [90s_dev] 分享了自己早期学习编程的经历，强调了重拾编程乐趣的愿望，类似于通过pico8重新体验到的感觉。
• [aidenn0] 认为Haskell代码比Lisp代码更易读，尽管两者都能通过注释理解功能，但对Lisp代码的冗长表示不满。
• [ninetyninenine] 高度评价Haskell的模块化特性，认为Haskell通过强制分离IO和纯函数实现了最高的模块化，并与其他编程范式进行了对比。
• [throwaway81523] 仅提到年份2011，未提供具体观点。
• [felineflock] 以幽默的方式比较了Smalltalk、Haskell和Lisp的编程风格，强调了不同语言的语法特点。
• [kazinator] 讨论了Common Lisp中使用对象和结构的冗长问题，并提出了TXR Lisp中的解决方案，同时对原文中的代码提出了改进建议。
• [jug] 表示对F#有兴趣，认为F#与其生态系统非常契合，尽管也欣赏Haskell的一些特性。
• [transfire] 对不同语言的实现都表示了一些不满，认为可读性与习惯有关，并提到FORTH可能是例外。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是Lisp语言的冗长和混乱问题，[wk_end]和[aidenn0]都提到了Lisp代码的冗长，而[kazinator]则提出了具体的简化建议。
• 另一个讨论点是Haskell的模块化特性，[ninetyninenine]认为Haskell的纯函数和类型系统提供了最高的模块化，而其他编程范式在这方面有所不足。
• 不同语言的语法和可读性也是讨论的重点，[felineflock]以幽默的方式比较了不同语言的语法特点，[xelxebar]和[0x445442]则对具体实现方式提出了看法。
• 最后，[transfire]提到可读性与习惯有关，并认为FORTH可能是一个例外，这为讨论提供了一个不同的视角。

44204878.article_content:
Daniel's Blog
Home
Archives
Search
Feed
About
To assist with job interviews at the
NRAO
we recently wrote a small
“
contest” program. Without giving away the details, the crux of the problem is to read a file with a list of scans and calculate the amount of time it takes to move the dishes and perform the scans, and report it. Candidates are required to write this in Java, but that restriction does not apply to me, so I of course had to write it in three languages that are not Java: Haskell, Common Lisp and Smalltalk.
I expect to learn something, or at least reinforce an existing fact, by doing these sorts of language games, but this time I really wasn’t expecting what I found. I discovered that my enjoyment of Haskell is pretty much independent of Haskell’s appropriateness or usability. In fact, it is more attributable to the way I feel when using it, in contrast to everything else. Let me show you a piece of code:
-- | Perform a scan and produce the scan log for it.
performScan ∷ Scan → AntennaSimulator ScanLog
performScan scan = wrapDuration $ do
slewTime     ← moveTo  $ scanPosition scan  -- move to the scan's position
onSourceTime ← waitFor $ scanLength   scan  -- wait for the scan to finish
return $ Log scan onSourceTime slewTime
Somehow, the other languages I’ve used to implement this problem never arrived at a piece of code quite this beautiful. Compare to the Smalltalk:
Scan ≫ runWith: anAntenna
runWith: anAntenna
"Performs this scan on the supplied antenna."
| onSourceTime slewTime |
slewTime     := anAntenna moveTo: self position; lastActionDuration.
onSourceTime := anAntenna wait: self duration; lastActionDuration.
^ ScanResult withScan: self slewTime: slewTime onSourceTime: onSourceTime
And the Lisp:
(defun run-scan (antenna scan)
"Perform a scan on this antenna. Return a scan log."
(let* ((slew-time       (move-to antenna (scan-position scan)))
(on-source-time  (delay antenna (scan-length scan)))
(total-time      (+ on-source-time slew-time)))
(with-slots (last-duration) antenna
(setf last-duration total-time)
(make-scan-log scan slew-time on-source-time))))
Strangely, despite the similarity of the Smalltalk, I still find the Haskell shorter and clearer. It’s also more modular, though it doesn’t look like it. The
wrapDuration
command arranges for the next set of actions to count as one as far as the
lastActionDuration
is concerned, but does not interfere with usages of
lastActionDuration
within the wrapped action. I found this notion essentially impossible to port to the other languages. The Haskell version really feels more like a composable set of actions for driving the antenna, whereas the Smalltalk version never really stopped feeling like an arithmetic fabrication, and the abstraction leaked a lot in the Lisp version
The Lisp code is just atrocious. I was never really able to put my finger on what it is I dislike about Lisp before. It’s this: while Lisp code is often clever and interesting, it also
always
feels like I’m tricking Lisp into doing what I want, rather than simply expressing what I want.
Neither Lisp nor Smalltalk really lend themselves to my style. I realize now, that my style is to try to break everything down into the smallest piece, a piece that doesn’t look like work. Haskell encourages this style with the
where
syntax, which encourages you to say, X is really Y + Z, with Y being this and Z being that. This kind of thing:
-- | To calculate the time to move between two positions, we take
-- whichever is larger of the time to turn and the time to change
-- elevation.
timeToMoveTo ∷ Position → Position → Time
timeToMoveTo (sourceAz, sourceEl) (destAz, destEl) =
max rotationTime ascensionTime
where
rotationTime, ascensionTime ∷ Time
rotationTime  = timeToRotate sourceAz destAz
ascensionTime = timeToAscend sourceEl destEl
This almost doesn’t look like code to me. I would expect any programmer to be able to at least get some sense of what’s going on here, even without knowing Haskell. I don’t think I could say the same thing about this piece of Lisp:
(defun time-to-move (from-pos to-pos)
"Calculates the total time to move between two positions, assuming
rotation and ascension can occur simultaneously."
(with-accessors ((from-az azimuth) (from-el elevation)) from-pos
(with-accessors ((to-az azimuth) (to-el elevation)) to-pos
(max (time-to-rotate from-az to-az) (time-to-ascend from-el to-el)))))
Lispers are fond of talking about the programmability of the syntax and how easy it is to learn. But the syntax is still there, it’s just encoded positionally rather than with auxiliary words and symbols. For example, the words
azimuth
and
elevation
in the Lisp code denote accessor functions. The outer
with-accessors
macro does something akin to this:
timeToMoveFrom: from_pos to: to_pos
| from_az from_el |
from_az := from_pos azimuth.
from_el := from_pos elevation.
...
So the Lisp is wonderfully terse, but I still feel like I’m tricking something into doing what I want rather than expres

data.title: Food additive titanium dioxide likely has more toxic effects than thought
data.author: Jimmc414
data.article_summary: 一篇新研究显示，食品添加剂二氧化钛（特别是纳米颗粒形式）可能具有比之前认为的更大的毒性，可能导致糖尿病和肥胖。该物质已在超11,000种美国产品中使用，包括M&M's糖果和Chips Ahoy饼干。研究发现，二氧化钛纳米颗粒会扰乱肠道激素，影响饱腹感信号和血糖调节，可能导致肥胖和糖尿病。欧盟已于2022年禁止其用于食品，但美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）仍认为其安全。公众健康组织已向FDA提交请愿书，要求禁止二氧化钛在食品中的使用，但尚未得到回应。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[含钛物质的潜在毒性及其在不同场景下的影响，尤其是植入物和日常消费品中的使用]

不同观点：
• [potamic] 认为钛植入物（如牙科或骨科植入物）会以较小速率腐蚀，释放出钛离子，这些离子会氧化形成二氧化钛颗粒，沉积在体内。尽管目前二氧化钛被认为无毒，但鉴于有新研究指出食物摄入途径的潜在毒性，长期植入物使用者可能面临风险。该评论提出了对长期健康影响的担忧，尤其是基于新研究结果。

• [ajb] 关注二氧化钛在其他消费品（如白色油漆）中的广泛使用，并将其与历史上铅基油漆的健康危害进行类比，表达了对二氧化钛潜在风险的警惕，担心可能重蹈覆辙。

• [genewitch] 对相关物质缺乏监管表示失望，暗示希望有政府机构采取行动禁止有害物质，但同时也表现出对实际监管行动的悲观态度。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于二氧化钛的实际毒性，尤其是在不同使用场景下的长期健康影响。新研究可能对当前认为无毒的物质提出挑战，特别是涉及长期植入物和日常消费品。

• 讨论还涉及对监管和公共健康政策的期望与失望，特别是对历史上类似事件（如铅基油漆）的联想，反映出公众对化学物质安全性的持续关注和不安。

• 不同观点之间的讨论关系表现为潜在健康风险的逐步扩展：从植入物使用者到广泛的消费品使用，再到对监管政策的期望。这显示出对同一物质在不同场景下健康影响的广泛关注。

US news
Food additive titanium dioxide likely has more toxic effects than thought, study finds
Controversial additive may be in as many as 11,000 US products and could lead to diabetes and obesity
Tom Perkins
Fri 6 Jun 2025 07.00 EDT
Last modified on Fri 6 Jun 2025 11.22 EDT
Share
The controversial food additive titanium dioxide likely has more toxic effects than previously thought, new peer-reviewed
research
shows, adding to growing evidence that unregulated nanoparticles used throughout the
food
system present an underestimated danger to consumers.
In nanoparticle form, titanium dioxide may throw off the body’s endocrine system by disrupting hormonal response to food and dysregulating blood sugar levels, which can lead to diabetes,
obesity
and other
health
problems, the study found.
Ultra-processed foods more broadly have this effect on “food hormones”, but there isn’t a full understanding of why, and the new research may help point to an answer.
FDA issues highest alert for tomato recall due to salmonella risk
Read more
“Our research highlights the detrimental effects of titanium dioxide nanoparticles as potential intestinal endocrine disruptors,” the authors wrote in the peer-reviewed study led by China’s Jiaxing Nanhu University.
Titanium dioxide in nanoparticle form is used in food to brighten whites or enhance colors, and may be in as many as 11,000 US products, especially candy and snack foods. Popular products like M&Ms and Chips Ahoy! cookies contain the substance. They’re also heavily used in nonstick ceramic pans.
The EU banned titanium dioxide for food use in 2022 because previous research has shown it to likely be a neurotoxin, be an immunotoxin, cause intestinal lesions and potentially damage genes. The particles can accumulate in organs and stay in the body for years. A 2022
lawsuit
drew wide attention for alleging that Skittles are “unfit for human consumption” because they contain titanium dioxide.
On the heels of the study, Skittles announced it would stop using the substance, while the US
Food
and Drug Administration (FDA) has maintained that it is safe.
The new research compared the gut health of three groups: mice that were fed titanium dioxide nanoparticles, mice that were fed larger microparticles and mice that were fed no titanium dioxide. Mice that were fed the nanoparticles showed lower levels of several types of gut hormones that signal to the body that it is full, aid in digestion and regulate glucose.
The mice that were fed the nanoparticles showed much higher levels of glucose, or blood sugar, than those that were fed microparticles. The authors also noted that “gut hormones secreted by enteroendocrine cells play a critical role regulating energy intake and maintaining glucose” levels. The titanium dioxide nanoparticles seemed to disrupt the enteroendocrine cells’ differentiation, which is part of the hormone secretion process, and reduce the cells’ numbers.
These issues can lead to obesity, type 2 diabetes and insulin resistance, the authors wrote.
The findings are “a really big deal because when you start messing with glucose levels – that’s diabetes”, said Tom Neltner, director of the non-profit Unleaded Kids, who, along with other public health groups, filed a formal petition with the FDA in 2023 that requested the agency ban the use of titanium dioxide in food.
The agency is legally compelled to respond within 180 days, but so far has ignored the petition, Neltner said. The petition comes as Robert F Kennedy Jr has made reducing toxic food additives a priority.
“He’s getting started so it’s too soon to tell, but there’s hope that we didn’t have before,” Neltner said. But he added that the groups will sue if the petition continues to be ignored.

44205895.article_summary: 一篇新研究显示，食品添加剂二氧化钛（特别是纳米颗粒形式）可能具有比之前认为的更大的毒性，可能导致糖尿病和肥胖。该物质已在超11,000种美国产品中使用，包括M&M's糖果和Chips Ahoy饼干。研究发现，二氧化钛纳米颗粒会扰乱肠道激素，影响饱腹感信号和血糖调节，可能导致肥胖和糖尿病。欧盟已于2022年禁止其用于食品，但美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）仍认为其安全。公众健康组织已向FDA提交请愿书，要求禁止二氧化钛在食品中的使用，但尚未得到回应。

44205060.article_content:
Elon Musk listens as President Donald Trump speaks in the Oval Office on Feb. 11, 2025.
Jim Watson / AFP - Getty Images file
June 6, 2025, 4:42 PM EDT
/
Updated
June 6, 2025, 7:49 PM EDT
By
Lawrence Hurley
and
Gary Grumbach
WASHINGTON — The
Supreme Court
on Friday allowed members of the Trump administration's Department of Government Efficiency to access Social Security Administration data.
The conservative-majority court, with its three liberal justices objecting, granted an emergency application filed by the Trump administration asking the justices to lift an injunction issued by a federal judge in Maryland.
The
unsigned order
said that members of the DOGE team assigned to the Social Security Administration should have "access to the agency records in question in order for those members to do their work."
The lawsuit challenging DOGE’s actions was filed by progressive group Democracy Forward on behalf of two unions — the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees, and the American Federation of Teachers — as well as the Alliance for Retired Americans.
"This is a sad day for our democracy and a scary day for millions of people," the groups said in a statement. "This ruling will enable President Trump and DOGE’s affiliates to steal Americans’ private and personal data."
The White House praised the ruling.
"The Supreme Court allowing the Trump Administration to carry out commonsense efforts to eliminate waste, fraud, and abuse and modernize government information systems is a huge victory for the rule of law," White House spokesperson Liz Huston said in a statement.
Follow live politics coverage here
Liberal Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson wrote a dissenting opinion questioning the need for the court to intervene on an emergency basis.
"In essence, the 'urgency' underlying the government’s stay application is the mere fact that it cannot be bothered to wait for the litigation process to play out before proceeding as it wishes," she added.
DOGE, set up by billionaire Elon Musk before his falling out with President Donald Trump,
says it wants to modernize systems and detect waste and fraud at the agency. The data it seeks includes Social Security numbers, medical records, and tax and banking information.
“These teams have a business need to access the data at their assigned agency and subject the government’s records to much-needed scrutiny,” Solicitor General D. John Sauer wrote in court papers.
The lawsuit alleged that allowing broader access to the personal information would violate a federal law called the Privacy Act as well as the Administrative Procedure Act.
"The agency is obligated by the Privacy Act and its own regulations, practices, and procedures to keep that information secure — and not to share it beyond the circle of those who truly need it," the challengers' lawyers wrote in court papers.
U.S. District Judge Ellen Hollander had ruled that DOGE had no need to access the specific data at issue. The 4th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, based in Richmond, Virginia, declined to block Hollander's decision, leading to the Trump administration to file its emergency request at the Supreme Court.
Social Security Administration Commissioner Frank Bisignano welcomed Friday's ruling by the high court.
“The Supreme Court’s ruling is a major victory for American taxpayers. The Social Security Administration will continue driving forward modernization efforts, streamlining government systems, and ensuring improved service and outcomes for our beneficiaries,” Bisignano said in a statement.
In a
separate order
issued Friday in another case involving DOGE, the Supreme Court granted another request filed by the Trump administration.
That decision allows the Trump administration to, for now, shield DOGE from freedom of information requests seeking thousands of pages of material.
The move
formalizes a decision
issued by Chief Justice John Roberts on May 23 that temporarily put lower court decisions on hold while the Supreme Court considered what next steps to take. The court also told lower courts to limit the scope of what material could be disclosed.
It means the government will not have to respond to requests for documents and allow for the deposition of the DOGE administrator, Amy Gleason, as a lower court had ruled, while litigation continues.
The three liberal justices noted their disagreement with that decision, too.
A spokesman for Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, which filed the lawsuit, said the group was "obviously disappointed" with the decision but "pleased that the court allowed discovery to proceed."
A Justice Department spokesman did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the order.
Lawrence Hurley
Lawrence Hurley is a senior Supreme Court reporter for NBC News.
Gary Grumbach
Gary Grumbach is a NBC News Legal Affairs Reporter, based in Washington, D.C.
Garrett Haake
and
Julia Jester
contributed
.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国最高法院允许社会保障管理局（SSA）向DOGE工作人员提供高度敏感的个人数据，引发的争议和讨论。

不同观点：
• [cycomanic] 引用了JUSTICE JACKSON的异议，认为法院在诉讼仍在进行时，不应批准政府紧急介入的请求。Jackson指出，政府未能证明如果不介入会造成不可挽回的伤害，且这种紧急介入不符合传统司法干预的标准。她将此视为法院在诉讼未决时的不当干预。

• [declan_roberts] 认为社会保障号码已经泄露，无法挽回，并批评银行在欺诈使用这些号码时将责任归咎于个人。这反映了公众对个人数据泄露的广泛担忧和不满。

• [0cf8612b2e1e] 质疑在法律问题未决时，允许DOGE完全访问数据的常见性，并认为在此情况下应默认最小化潜在伤害，即保持数据锁定。

• [e40] 提到Elon Musk与DOGE的关系，质疑Musk是否通过DOGE获取数据和操控结果，这涉及到可能的利益冲突和数据安全问题。

• [quantified] 提到DOGE拥有IRS数据，并暗示这可能被用于政治谈判，如Musk与Trump之间的谈判，这引发了对数据被滥用于政治目的的担忧。

补充讨论：
• [JumpCrisscross] 和 [laristine] 提供了相关法院命令和存档链接，为讨论提供了具体参考。

• [zingababba] 猜测这些数据将被存储在一个向量数据库中，暗示对数据用途的进一步技术性推测。

• [vaxman] 认为此决定不会带来实际节省，且预测此举会带来政治责任，最终可能被特朗普政府撤销，并提到未来可能采取的财政紧缩措施。

争议焦点：
• 核心争议在于在诉讼未决时，是否应允许DOGE访问敏感数据，以及这种访问是否会带来不可挽回的伤害或被滥用。

data.title: Our kids are under surveillance: The hidden privacy crisis in Ed Tech
data.author: matteogauthier
data.article_summary: 文章揭示了自2020年疫情以来，许多用于远程教育的教育科技（Ed Tech）应用和网站存在窃取学生隐私的问题。研究显示，高达96%的美国学校使用的教育应用与第三方分享学生信息，其中78%与广告商和数据经纪公司共享数据。全球49个国家的164个教育科技产品中，89%嵌入了向广告行业报告的跟踪器。平均每个教育科技应用会将数据转发给6.7家不同的数据经纪公司，包括位置信息、生物识别数据、个人社交信息、行为数据及敏感记录等。这些数据常被用于广告和用户画像，严重威胁学生隐私。文章呼吁加强保护儿童隐私，并建议采取更注重隐私的教育方式。

44204670.article_content:
Published on June 6, 2025
In 2020, there was a rush to connect students to remote classrooms during the pandemic. In the years since, we’ve discovered most education apps and websites (referred to as Ed Tech) and platforms are spying on our children
.
In 2022, Researchers at the Internet Safety Labs found that up to
96% of apps used in US schools
(new window)
share student information with third parties
, and 78% of them shared this data with advertisers and data brokers. Human Rights Watch’s (HRW)
2022
global analysis of 164 Ed Tech products
(new window)
across 49 countries revealed that
89% of them risk children’s privacy
by embedding trackers that report back to the advertising industry. Another study by the Internet Safety Labs, this one published in 2024, found that the average Ed Tech app with trackers
forwarded data to 6.7 different data broker companies
(new window)
every time a student logged on. This means every students’ click, keystroke, and physical location can be traced by companies with commercial motives — often without parents or teachers even knowing.
The findings from all these studies are remarkably consistent. Most Ed Tech services collect far more student data than parents and schools realize.
What data do Ed Tech apps collect?
How is this data used?
Why this matters
Students, teachers, and parents are speaking up
How to protect your child’s privacy
A privacy-first education
What data do Ed Tech apps collect?
The scope of information Ed Tech services access and collect is broad. In particularly egregious cases, some Ed Tech services were caught secretly collecting students’ information. This behavior is unacceptable for any app, especially one that schools require children to use.
Examples of the sensitive data these apps collect include:
Location data:
Many apps can track students’ precise GPS location or IP-based whereabouts. As
HRW
(new window)
warns, such data can reveal
“
where a child lives and where they go to school, trips between divorced parents’ homes, and visits to a doctor’s office specializing in childhood cancer
”
.
Biometric and media access:
Many virtual classroom tools need access to cameras, microphones, and even keyboards so children can talk to their teachers or share answers. But there’s no need for an app to share this information with third parties. Adobe Connect, for instance, was found logging keystrokes and phone numbers; accessing students’ cameras and microphones; and
sharing this information with Google
(new window)
.
Personal and social data:
Many education apps ask for or harvest contact lists, email addresses, and demographic information. HRW found three
particularly egregious apps
(new window)
(Kelas Pintar, Shad, and Extramarks) that collected this information without disclosing it in their privacy policies. This ability to map social networks is extremely valuable, and something all data brokers try to do.
Behavior and usage data:
Every click, quiz answer, or timestamp is often logged. Ed Tech systems capture what pages students visit, how long they spend on tasks, and which problems they struggle with. Alone this sounds benign, but when combined with third-party trackers, it can be correlated with behavior outside school.
Sensitive records:
Some learning apps inevitably touch on private subjects. For example, online counseling tools, mental health quizzes, or special education resources could reveal health conditions or disabilities. An Internet Safety Labs report found that
mental health records
(new window)
and similarly sensitive information were being shared with ad networks.
For most Ed Tech services, no data source is too sensitive or off limits. Advertising trackers embedded in school apps can log everything from your child’s reading level to the names of their siblings. The worry is that companies then aggregate these details into profiles, essentially creating a dossier on your child.
Sophisticated ad-tech firms can combine students’ school data with the data they collect from social media and e-marketers to target children and their families, predict behavior, and influence minds that are still taking shape.
How is this data used?
In the vast majority of cases, students’ sensitive data is used to fuel the advertising and profiling industries. When children’s devices ping dozens of ad trackers, that information typically goes to marketing platforms, analytics firms, and data brokers. 44201527.article_content:
You've most likely heard about
gradient noise
through the name
Perlin
noise
, which refers to one particular implementation with various CPU
optimizations. Because it's an incredible tool for creative work, it's used
virtually everywhere: visual effects, video games, procedural mathematical art,
etc. While getting it right can sometimes be subtle, a "broken" implementation
can still look good or interesting. After all, "it looks fine, and I'm an
artist".
In order to gain a deeper and more meaningful understanding we will start
studying the 1D version (a case often omitted in the literature), then slowly
climb our way up in dimensions and complexity. We'll also work from a GPU
perspective rather than a CPU-based one, hence all code snippets and visuals
here are implemented in WebGL2/GLSL (hopefully without being too heavy on
performance). They should run on most modern devices; let me know if you run
into issues.
Before we begin, credit where it's due: most of the material here are nothing
new. This article is the result of weeks of studying and experimenting with
the maths from
Inigo Quilez's incredible pages
and other scattered
resources over the Internet. But as rich and valuable these resources are, they
sometimes move quickly over the details, assuming they're obvious. This post is
an attempt to fill those gaps.
A welcoming wavy 1D gradient noise signal
Hashing function and pseudo-random values
At the most elementary level, we need a deterministic coordinate based
pseudo-random system. More specifically, for any given integer coordinate we
need a random value, and as uniformly distributed as possible. Something like:
\begin{aligned}
h(-3) &= -0.006124 \\
h(-2) &= -0.996686 \\
h(-1) &= 0.200864 \\
h(0) &= -1.000000 \\
h(1) &= 0.053313 \\
h(2) &= -0.893312 \\
h(3) &= 0.854923 \\
\text{...}
\end{aligned}
Perlin's implementation relies on a permutation table, which is convenient when
working on the CPU, but more awkward for a shader. On the GPU, most people rely
on various floating point hacks or sub-optimal bit tricks, which often fall
short when exploring the full 32-bit range of inputs.
Note
We can not use a PRNG because it relies on a state where we need determinism
(for one coordinate, we always want the same random value). LCG (Linear
Congruential Generator) are a sub-classes of PRNG where the state is
actually the returned value. But even then, we can not re-use the previously
returned value since we need seeking; that is the ability to get the random
value associated with our integer coordinate. Trying to feed a PRNG/LCG with
our coordinate instead of the expected state would be equivalent to changing
the seed at every call, and this may create an important bias in the random
distribution. This is the reason why we need integer hashing instead.
So we need a hashing function, and we will have to limit ourselves to
32-bit because we're on the GPU. Fortunately, we won't have to look for
very long because in 2018
Chris Wellons found a pretty good one he named
lowbias32
, which was later
refined by TheIronBorn
.
This is the first building block we will be using, the hashing function:
uint hash(uint x) {
x = (x ^ (x >> 16)) * 0x21f0aaadU;
x = (x ^ (x >> 15)) * 0x735a2d97U;
return x ^ (x >> 15);
}
This is sweet and all, but a 32-bit unsigned integer is not directly useful by
itself, we need a normalized float. We could naively divide by
0xffffffff
,
but we'll end up with a nonuniform distribution (this is not as important as it
may sound to be honest). Instead, we will adapt the
technique presented by
Vigna Sebastiano for doubles
to floats, and in GLSL:
float u2f(uint x) { return float(x >> 8U) * uintBitsToFloat(0x33800000U); }
Combining these two functions into
u2f(hash(x))
maps any 32-bit
coordinate
x
to a random float in
[0,1)
.
To match our
h(x)
function from earlier and make it more "signal-like", we can
optionally center it around
0
by remapping it from
[0,1)
to
[-1,1)
:
h(x)=u2f(hash(x))*2.0-1.0
.
Expanding the hash function to more dimensions
When we will work in 2 or more dimensions, our input grid coordinates will be
more than one value, but we need a way to feed them to our single parameter hash
function. One trick is to use nested xor hash:
uint hash(uvec2 x) { return hash(x.x ^ hash(x.y)); }  // for 2D input
uint hash(uvec3 x) { return hash(x.x ^ hash(x.yz)); } // for 3D input
Using the pixel coordinates as input, we can test the hashing function in 2D:
float stepnoise2(vec2 p) {
ivec2 i = ivec2(floor(p));    // integer coordinate, or lattice
return u2f(hash(uvec2(i)));   // non-centered h(x)
}
Display h(x,y) by stepping the contiguous coordinates
Warning
We're going through an intermediate signed integer conversion before going
to unsigned to avoid issues with negative coordinates. Quoting GLSL 4.60
specifications: "It is undefined to convert a negative floating-point value
to an uint". With this conversion we will only have a problem when the
coordinates go outside the signed 32-bit range.
B

data.title: Falsehoods programmers believe about aviation
data.author: cratermoon
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了FlightAware在处理航空数据时遇到的复杂和非标准化情况。尽管希望数据是干净和标准化的，但现实中存在许多误解和错误假设，包括航班离港时间、标识、机场代码以及导航数据等方面。例如，航班不一定按计划时间离港，可能有多个航班号，机场代码可能不唯一，ADS-B消息的准确性也存在问题。FlightAware的Hyperfeed引擎需要正确解读这些情况，以提供一致的数据反馈。文章强调了在设计航空数据系统时需考虑的异常情况和现实世界的复杂性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：程序员对航空领域的一些误解以及航空标识符和飞行数据的复杂性

不同观点：
• [sixdimensional] 认为飞机没有一个随时间不变（time invariant）的唯一标识符，唯一能标识飞机整个生命周期的是制造商、型号和序列号的组合。他还指出，注册号和尾号可能会改变，而ICAO 24位地址可以重新编程。
• [EMM_386] 对[sixdimensional]提到的程序员误解表示困惑，尤其对跑道编号因地球磁场变化而改变表示不解，并质疑为何特别指出程序员会有这些误解。
• [FabHK] 认为这类列表缺乏深入解释，虽然有些声明有链接支持，但未详细说明事件背景，例如某个航班准时起飞但延迟40小时到达。
• [bnycum] 从事飞行数据记录器开发，提到在处理直升机等飞行器的数据时，日常工作中经常遇到各种关于航空的误解。
• [genocidicbunny] 指出，许多程序员倾向于认为人类设计的系统会严格遵循规则，而忽略了边缘情况。
• [ryandrake] 认为这些“程序员误解”列表应作为测试的来源，每个项目都应生成单元测试或集成测试，以纠正错误的假设。
• [marcosdumay] 提到巴西航空系统的老旧计算机系统曾对一些航空异常进行修复，并指出跑道和机场不会移动，且机场和跑道的变动通常会事先有施工工作。
• [Titan2189] 推荐CGP Grey的视频，解释机场代码的混乱情况。
• [dtgriscom] 提到在FlightAware论坛上也有类似讨论。
• [aryehof] 建议制作一个真实约束的列表，以与虚假约束对比，并询问是否有一种符号可以表示这些约束。
• [usui] 对“航班”的抽象概念感到困惑，质疑当一个新航班创建时意味着什么。
• [throwaway290] 开玩笑地说“飞机降落”是最短的误解。
• [zzo38computer] 提到有些机场有ICAO代码但没有IATA代码，或有“伪ICAO”代码。
• [sandwic101] 认为这些误解类似于其他领域的边缘情况，并以汽车和道路为例，说明每个领域都有类似的问题。

补充讨论：
• 关于飞机唯一标识符的复杂性以及相关例子（如注册号、尾号、ICAO地址）是主要技术争议点。
• 讨论中涉及对机场代码、跑道编号变化以及航班定义的困惑和解释需求。
• 一些评论提到了对系统规则和边缘情况的处理方式，以及如何通过测试纠正误解。

44205590.article_content:
At FlightAware, our software needs to gracefully handle all sorts of weird and wonderful situations. While we as engineers might hope for aviation data to be clean and well-standardized, the real world is messy.
There are a lot of assumptions one could make when designing data types and schemas for aviation data that turn out to be inaccurate. In the spirit of
Patrick McKenzie’s classic piece on names
, here are some false assumptions one might make about aviation. While many of these are simply common misconceptions, some of these assumptions have bitten our customers at various points, and others have caused issues in our own systems over the years.
Together they are illustrative of the situations that Hyperfeed, our flight tracking engine, is responsible for correctly interpreting in order to provide a clean and consistent data feed for our website, apps, and APIs.
Flights
Flights depart from a gate
Flights that depart from a gate
only leave their gate once
Flights depart within a few hours of the time they were scheduled to
Flights depart
within a day
of the time they were scheduled to
Flights have schedules
Flights take off and land
at airports
Airplanes (excluding helicopters) take off and land at airports
Flights are at most
a dozen or so hours long
Okay, they’re at most
a few days long
Flights are identified by a flight number consisting of an airline’s code plus some numbers, like UAL1234
Flights
are identified by either
an airline flight number like UAL1234, or the aircraft’s registration like N12345, B6459, or FHUVL
A flight identifier like B6459 is unambiguously either a registration (
B–6459
), an airline flight number (
B6 459
), or something else
Flights don’t have
multiple flight numbers
Flights with multiple flight numbers unambiguously have one “main” flight number
A particular trip’s flight number(s)
never change
The flight number shown on your ticket
is what the pilots and air traffic control are using
Flights don’t use the code of some entirely unrelated airline in their flight identifier
No flights use the same flight number within a day
Surely at least no flights use the same flight number at the same time?
Okay fine, separate flights from the same major passenger airline that depart within a few minutes of each other would not
both
have the
same
flight number… right?
Airports
Airports
never move
Terminal and gate numbers have a consistent naming scheme
Each runway is
only used by one
airport
Airports always have two unique identifiers: a 4-letter Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) code and a 3-letter International Air Transport Association (IATA) code
Airports always have three unique identifiers: an ICAO, an IATA, and a regionally-administered location code
The U.S. Department of Transportation
assigns one
canonical code to
each airport
it oversees
No airports have
multiple IATA codes
The ICAO code for airports in the U.S.
always starts with the letter K
For U.S. airports whose ICAO code starts with K, the
last three letters
are its IATA code
You can tell which
geographic region
an airport is in from its ICAO code
Everything that has an IATA code
is an airport
Everything that has an ICAO code
is on Earth
Airports have at least one well-known identifier of some sort
Airlines
No
two
airlines
share
the same
IATA code
No
airlines
use
multiple
IATA or ICAO
codes
You can tell
what airline is operating a flight
by looking at the physical aircraft
Airlines assign flight numbers to specific routes
Airlines only assign flight numbers to
flights they operate
Airlines only assign flight numbers to
flights
Navigation
Waypoint names are unique
There is one
agreed-upon definition of altitude
Flight information from Air Navigation Service Providers is accurate
Okay,
pretty
accurate; they wouldn’t indicate that a flight had departed unless it really had
If they indicate that a flight plan has been cancelled, then that flight definitely isn’t going to operate — it wouldn’t simply be due to someone editing the flight plan
At least their radar data accurately identifies each aircraft
Radars with overlapping coverage areas agree on the location of a target they can both see
If they send us a flight plan with the ICAO identifier of a known airport as the destination, then there must have been some intention of arriving there
If an aircraft diverts to another destination, it won’t
divert again
Transponders and ADS-B
ADS-B messages only come from aircraft
ADS-B messages only come from aircraft and airport service vehicles
ADS-B messages only come from vehicles of some kind
The GPS position in ADS-B messages
is accurate
The GPS position in ADS-B messages is accurate
within some known uncertainty
radius
ADS-B messages always include the correct flight identification
Transponders are correctly programmed to indicate the aircraft type (helicopter, airplane, balloon, etc)
You can always determine a aircraft’s registration number from its ADS-B messages
Transponders are programmed with the correct Mode S address
